growth_003:n1.prompt:
You are helping me set up an email marketing account as the first step in configuring our email marketing system (audience, templates, and welcome automation come later). {{vendor}} is our chosen provider for this role.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) my business/brand name, (2) the domain I want associated with this account, (3) the email address I want to use as the account owner/login, and (4) any preferred company details (address, industry) that signup forms typically request.

Once you have these, go to {{vendor}}'s signup page and fill in the account creation form fields: business name, domain, owner email, password field (leave blank or use placeholder text — do not generate or enter a password on my behalf), and any company profile fields requested. Prepare all of this as a pre-filled draft so I can review it quickly.

Do not submit the form, do not verify the email, and do not accept any terms of service or account agreements — creating the account and accepting {{vendor}}'s terms must be done by me personally as the legal account holder, and email verification is something only I can complete. This remains a human step.

When you're done, report back with: a checklist of all the fields you've drafted and their values, a direct link to the {{vendor}} signup page, and a clear note confirming the draft is ready and that you are stopping here — stop for human sign-off before I create the account, verify my email, and accept the terms myself.

growth_003:n2.prompt:
You are helping me set up the audience list for our email marketing platform ({{vendor}}) as part of our onboarding. If you don't already have it, ask me for: (1) my {{vendor}} account credentials context (assume you can use your configured credentials), (2) a plain-language description of who should be in the audience (e.g., signups, leads, customers, and any tags or custom properties like plan tier, signup source, or lifecycle stage), and (3) any existing contact data source (CSV, CRM export, or API) I want imported.

Please do the following:
1. Draft the audience list structure: list name, required fields, and any custom properties/tags needed to support segmentation described above.
2. Translate my plain-language audience description into concrete segment definitions (based on profile attributes, tags, or behavioral events) that {{vendor}} can maintain live as data changes.
3. Prepare the contact creation flow: show exactly how a sample contact would be added using {{vendor}}'s contact creation endpoint (POST /contacts/create), including field mappings for custom properties.
4. If I provided a data source, prepare a batch import plan (mapping fields, deduplication rules) but do not execute the import yet.
5. Produce a summary checklist showing: list name, segment definitions, custom fields, and the sample API call payload for contact creation.

Do not create the live audience list, add real contacts, or run any import in {{vendor}} yet — a human must explicitly approve before any changes are applied. Prepare everything so it's ready to execute in one step once approved, and then stop for human sign-off.

Report back with the full checklist, segment definitions, sample payload, and any open questions I need to answer before you can finalize the setup.

growth_003:n3.prompt:
You are helping me create email templates in {{vendor}} as part of setting up email marketing. Before starting, ask me for anything you don't already have: my {{vendor}} account access (confirm you can use my configured credentials), my domain/brand name, links or files for brand assets (logo, colors, fonts), and a brief describing the types of emails I need templates for (e.g., welcome email, newsletter, promotional). If I have existing copy or a rough draft, ask for that too.

Once you have the inputs, do the following inside {{vendor}}: (1) Use the platform's built-in AI drafting/refining tool to propose subject lines and body copy for each requested template based on my brief, so I can review before anything is finalized. (2) Use the visual editor to design on-brand layouts for each template, incorporating my brand assets and personalization tokens (e.g., first name) so they render correctly across major email clients. (3) If I've indicated a preference for code-managed templates, prepare HTML or MJML source with variable placeholders instead, structured so it could be tracked in version control.

Save all templates as drafts only — do not activate, publish, or link them to any live automation or campaign. When done, give me a summary listing each template's name/purpose, a preview or screenshot link if available, and the draft subject line and copy for each. Since a human must explicitly approve before changes are applied, stop for human sign-off once drafts are prepared — do not publish, send, or activate anything without my explicit approval.

growth_003:n4.prompt:
You are helping me set up the welcome automation for our email marketing program using {{vendor}}. If you don't already have them, ask me for: my {{vendor}} account access confirmation (I'll say I've configured credentials), the target audience/list name, the welcome email content or key messaging points, the event or signal that should trigger the automation (e.g. a signup or custom product event), the desired timing/delays between steps, any branching logic (e.g. based on user attributes or engagement), and exit rules (conditions under which someone should leave the flow).

Using this, draft a complete welcome automation plan: the trigger, each step in the sequence with its delay, any branches, and exit conditions. If the trigger is a custom event fired from our product, prepare the integration using {{vendor}}'s event-sending API (an operation like sending an event payload to trigger the workflow, e.g. a call similar to POST /events/send) — describe exactly what event name and payload fields our system should send, but do not execute the send yourself.

Build the automation as a draft/inactive workflow inside {{vendor}} so I can review it, and prepare a way to identify and manage individual contacts within the flow (so I can see where someone sits and pull or re-enter them if needed). Do not activate, publish, or turn on the automation, and do not send any live emails or events.

When done, report back: a summary of the automation steps/branches/exit rules as configured, the exact event name and payload structure needed for the trigger, and a link or reference to the draft workflow in {{vendor}}. Then stop for human sign-off before any activation or changes are applied.

growth_003:n5.prompt:
You are helping me configure the signup form for our email marketing audience in {{vendor}}. Human sign-off is required before anything goes live, so your job is to prepare everything and then stop.

First, ask me for anything you need that isn't already available: our target audience/list name in {{vendor}}, a plain-language description of who should be able to sign up (the segment/audience definition), the fields we want to collect (e.g., email, first name, custom properties), and any branding or welcome copy preferences for the form.

Then, using your configured credentials and {{vendor}}'s documented API:
1. Translate my plain-language audience description into a concrete segment definition (tags, custom fields, or list criteria) suitable for {{vendor}}.
2. Draft the signup form configuration: fields to capture, required vs optional, any tags/custom properties to attach to new contacts, and confirmation/welcome messaging.
3. Confirm how new signups will be created — new contacts should be added via the audience member-creation endpoint (Create a new contact/member for an audience via signup form submission) so I can verify the mapping of form fields to contact properties.
4. Prepare a checklist summarizing: audience/list target, segment/tag logic, form fields, and what happens to a contact upon submission (including suppression rules if someone unsubscribes or already exists).
5. Do NOT create, update, or activate anything live — only prepare drafts, configuration payloads, and a clear summary for review.

When done, report back with: the audience/list you targeted, the full field/tag mapping, the segment logic in plain language, and the draft signup form configuration. Explicitly state that you have not applied any changes and that this is ready for review — then stop for human sign-off.
